questions.stem: To understand how temperature change affects microorganism-mediated cycling of soil nutrients in alpine ecosystems, Eva Kaštovská et al. collected plant-soil cores in the Tatra Mountains at elevations around 2,100 meters and transplanted them to elevations of 1,700–1,800 meters, where the mean air temperature was warmer by 2°C. Microorganism- mediated nutrient cycling was accelerated in the transplanted cores; crucially, microorganism community composition was unchanged, allowing Kaštovská et al. to attribute the acceleration to temperature-induced increases in microorganism activity. It can most reasonably be inferred from the text that the finding about the microorganism community composition was important for which reason?

options.A: It provided preliminary evidence that microorganism-mediated nutrient cycling was accelerated in the transplanted cores.
options.B: It suggested that temperature-induced changes in microorganism activity may be occurring at increasingly high elevations.
options.C: It ruled out a potential alternative explanation for the acceleration in microorganism-mediated nutrient cycling.
options.D: It clarified that microorganism activity levels in the plant-soil cores varied depending on which microorganisms comprised the community

questions.stem: A bookstore moved a display of staff-recommended novels from a back aisle to a table near the entrance. The books' prices and recommendation cards did not change, but sales of the displayed titles increased during the following month. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: A display's visibility can influence which books customers purchase.
options.B: Customers buy recommended books only when their prices are reduced.
options.C: Staff recommendations are ineffective unless placed in a back aisle.
options.D: The bookstore added new titles to the display during the month.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The change in location, with price and recommendation wording held constant, implies that visibility contributed to the sales increase.

questions.stem: A theater offered captioned performances of a play on two additional evenings. The number of returning patrons was similar to that at noncaptioned performances, but the captioned performances attracted substantially more first-time patrons. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Returning patrons dislike captioned performances.
options.B: The theater sold fewer tickets after adding captions.
options.C: Captions may have reduced a barrier that had kept some new patrons from attending.
options.D: First-time patrons attended only because the tickets were less expensive.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The increase specifically among first-time patrons implies that captions made attendance more accessible to some people.

questions.stem: Fossilized teeth from juvenile members of an extinct mammal species show little surface wear, whereas adult teeth from the same sites show heavy grinding wear. Other skeletal evidence indicates that the animals' habitat remained stable during this period. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Juveniles and adults lived in different climates.
options.B: The species likely shifted to a more abrasive diet as individuals matured.
options.C: Adults replaced all their teeth immediately after reaching maturity.
options.D: Habitat change caused the adults' tooth wear.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The age-related wear difference, combined with stable habitat evidence, implies a dietary shift as the animals matured.

questions.stem: An orchestra performed the same composition in an indoor hall and at two outdoor venues. The musicians used nearly identical tempos indoors and outdoors on calm evenings, but they played more slowly outdoors when strong wind was present. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The orchestra had never rehearsed the composition indoors.
options.B: Outdoor audiences always prefer slower performances.
options.C: Strong wind made the composition shorter.
options.D: The musicians adjusted their interpretation in response to performance conditions.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The tempo changed specifically under windy conditions, implying that the musicians adapted to the environment.

questions.stem: Farmers in one mountain region record both fixed calendar dates and the flowering dates of a native shrub. In years when the rainy season begins unusually early or late, the shrub's flowering date predicts the start of the rains more accurately than the calendar date does. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Local biological cues can be useful when seasonal timing varies from year to year.
options.B: The shrub flowers on the same calendar date every year.
options.C: Calendar records are always more accurate than observations of plants.
options.D: Farmers in the region do not record rainfall.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The shrub's variable flowering date tracks variable rainy-season timing better than a fixed date, implying the value of biological cues.

questions.stem: Analysis of paintings from a seventeenth-century workshop found that an expensive blue pigment appeared mainly in thin final layers. Less costly pigments were used in the thicker layers underneath, even where the finished surface appeared blue. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The painters did not know how to mix blue pigment.
options.B: The underlying pigments were more expensive than the surface pigment.
options.C: The workshop conserved a costly material while preserving the desired visible color.
options.D: Every layer of each painting was intended to remain visible.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Concentrating the expensive pigment in visible final layers implies an effort to economize without sacrificing appearance.

questions.stem: A transit agency tested two station maps: one labeled exits with text only, and one used both text and widely recognized icons. Native speakers of the local language navigated equally quickly with either map, but visitors who spoke other languages navigated faster with the icon-enhanced map. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Native speakers are unable to interpret station icons.
options.B: Icons can make navigation information more accessible across language differences.
options.C: Visitors ignored all text on the icon-enhanced map.
options.D: Text-only maps are faster for every group of traveler.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The icon-enhanced map specifically improved navigation for visitors who spoke other languages, implying greater cross-language accessibility.

questions.stem: A café moved its unsweetened drinks to the first page of the menu while leaving prices and recipes unchanged. Orders of those drinks increased during the next month. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Menu placement can influence customers' selections.
options.B: The café reduced the price of every unsweetened drink.
options.C: Customers stopped reading the first page of the menu.
options.D: Recipe changes caused the increase in orders.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Only menu placement changed, implying that presentation affected choices.

questions.stem: A clinic began sending appointment reminders that included a direct link for rescheduling. Missed appointments declined, and more patients rescheduled at least a day in advance. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The reminders increased the number of missed appointments.
options.B: Making rescheduling easier helped patients notify the clinic instead of simply missing visits.
options.C: Patients could no longer reschedule by phone.
options.D: Every patient attended at the original appointment time.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The paired decline in missed visits and rise in advance rescheduling implies the mechanism.

questions.stem: A park replaced text-heavy trail signs with signs that combined brief text and pictograms. International visitors asked rangers for directions less often, while local visitors' behavior changed little. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Local visitors could not understand the new signs.
options.B: Rangers removed all text from every sign.
options.C: Pictograms made the trail information easier to use across language differences.
options.D: International visitors stopped using park trails.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The change primarily helped visitors likely to face language barriers.

questions.stem: Pottery fragments from several workshops carry distinctive maker's marks. At a distant trading center, archaeologists found vessels bearing marks from all those workshops. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: All workshops used exactly the same mark.
options.B: The trading center produced every marked vessel locally.
options.C: Maker's marks prevented pottery from being traded.
options.D: The trading center received pottery from multiple production locations.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Different workshop marks at one distant site imply multiple sources.

questions.stem: An online course added captions to all lectures. Completion rates rose most among students studying in noisy shared spaces, even though the lecture audio did not change. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Captions helped some students follow lectures when listening conditions were poor.
options.B: Captions made the audio louder.
options.C: Students in quiet rooms were prohibited from using captions.
options.D: Noisy spaces became silent after captions were added.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The strongest effect occurred where audio was harder to use.

questions.stem: An aquarium gradually dimmed exhibit lights during the final hour before closing. Nocturnal fish became active earlier, and visitors reported seeing behaviors that had previously occurred after the building closed. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Nocturnal fish are active only under bright light.
options.B: Lighting conditions can be adjusted to make nocturnal behavior visible during visitor hours.
options.C: The aquarium extended its closing time.
options.D: Visitors entered the building after it closed.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Earlier activity under dimmer light implies a practical exhibit-design effect.

questions.stem: A city added flexible posts between a bicycle lane and parked cars. Reports of cars entering the lane fell, although the width and route of the lane stayed the same. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The city widened the bicycle lane.
options.B: The posts caused more cars to enter the lane.
options.C: A visible physical separator discouraged drivers from entering the bicycle lane.
options.D: Drivers stopped parking on the street entirely.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The separator was the relevant change associated with fewer intrusions.

questions.stem: An orchestra began recording rehearsals and reviewing short excerpts at the next practice. Musicians corrected balance problems earlier in the rehearsal cycle, though total rehearsal time did not increase. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Recordings lengthened every rehearsal.
options.B: The musicians stopped listening to one another during performances.
options.C: Balance problems can be detected only by an audience.
options.D: Listening to recordings helped the orchestra identify issues that were not fully apparent while playing.

questions.explanation: D is correct. Earlier correction without more rehearsal time implies diagnostic value from playback.

questions.stem: A grocery store introduced smaller carts beside its standard carts. Shoppers buying only a few items selected the smaller carts most often and spent less time waiting to return carts after checkout. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Offering cart sizes matched to different trips can improve convenience for small purchases.
options.B: Small-cart users purchased more than every standard-cart user.
options.C: The store removed all standard carts.
options.D: Cart size changed the prices of groceries.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Use by small-trip shoppers and shorter return waits imply improved convenience.

questions.stem: An astronomy club covered flashlights with red filters during observing sessions. Members needed less time to readjust to the dark after checking star charts. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Red filters made the sky brighter.
options.B: Red-filtered light disturbed members' night vision less than ordinary flashlight light had.
options.C: Members stopped using star charts.
options.D: Dark adaptation is unrelated to light exposure.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Faster readjustment implies less disruption to dark adaptation.

questions.stem: After a local archive digitized its most fragile newspapers, researchers consulted the digital copies frequently while requests to handle the originals declined. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Digitization prevented researchers from reading the newspapers.
options.B: The originals became stronger after scanning.
options.C: Digital access can support research while reducing wear on delicate originals.
options.D: Researchers preferred to damage physical newspapers.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Greater digital use paired with reduced handling implies both access and preservation benefits.

questions.stem: A plaza fountain was programmed to operate during the hottest afternoon hours rather than early morning. More visitors gathered near it in the afternoon, but morning use of the plaza remained similar. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The fountain caused morning temperatures to rise.
options.B: Morning visitors stopped using the plaza.
options.C: The plaza was closed during the afternoon.
options.D: Scheduling the fountain for hotter hours increased its value as an afternoon gathering feature.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The timing change affected afternoon gathering without reducing morning use.

questions.stem: In a row of otherwise similar buildings, roofs coated with a pale material were cooler at midday than dark roofs. Indoor temperatures differed most on the top floors. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Roof color and reflectance can have the greatest indoor effect close to the roof.
options.B: Dark roofs prevented sunlight from reaching the buildings.
options.C: Ground floors were always hotter than top floors.
options.D: Roof coatings changed the number of floors in each building.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The strongest difference near the roof implies where the surface treatment matters most.

questions.stem: Seed packets were redesigned to show both planting depth and a simple depth diagram. Novice gardeners made fewer planting-depth errors, while experienced gardeners' results were unchanged. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Experienced gardeners could not interpret the diagram.
options.B: A visual planting guide was especially useful to gardeners with less experience.
options.C: The packets contained different seeds after redesign.
options.D: Novice gardeners planted at random more often.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The benefit concentrated among novices implies that the diagram supplied missing procedural knowledge.

questions.stem: A museum added touchable scale models beside several sculptures that visitors were not permitted to touch. Visitors with visual impairments spent more time at those displays and described the sculptures' forms more accurately. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The museum allowed visitors to touch the original sculptures.
options.B: Scale models made every sculpture larger.
options.C: Tactile models provided spatial information that visual access alone could not provide to some visitors.
options.D: Visitors with visual impairments spent less time at the displays.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The targeted gains imply improved access to form through touch.

questions.stem: A messaging application changed its default so that new accounts shared location data only after users actively enabled the feature. Far fewer new users shared location data, although the option remained available. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The application removed location sharing entirely.
options.B: Every user actively enabled the feature.
options.C: Location data became more accurate after the change.
options.D: Default settings strongly influence whether users activate a privacy-related feature.

questions.explanation: D is correct. The large behavior change despite unchanged availability implies a default effect.

questions.stem: A bus system installed interior displays showing the next three stops. Requests for stop information declined most on routes used heavily by tourists. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Advance stop displays reduced uncertainty for riders unfamiliar with a route.
options.B: Tourists stopped riding the buses.
options.C: Drivers removed stop names from the route.
options.D: Regular riders asked more questions because of the displays.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The strongest reduction on tourist-heavy routes implies help for unfamiliar riders.

questions.stem: A community garden introduced an online tool-reservation calendar. Conflicts over shared tools decreased, even though the number of tools did not change. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The garden purchased twice as many tools.
options.B: Coordinating access can reduce competition for limited equipment without increasing supply.
options.C: Gardeners stopped using shared equipment.
options.D: Reservation calendars create more scheduling conflicts.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The same supply produced fewer conflicts after coordination improved.

questions.stem: A restaurant served the same portions on slightly smaller plates for one week. Customers left less food uneaten, while the number of additional orders did not change. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The restaurant reduced every portion.
options.B: Smaller plates caused customers to order more food.
options.C: Plate size influenced how customers perceived or consumed an unchanged portion.
options.D: Food waste increased during the trial.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Because portion size and extra orders were stable, the plate presentation likely affected consumption.

questions.stem: A school installed water-bottle filling stations near its gym and cafeteria. Students refilled bottles more often, and purchases of single-use bottled water declined. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The filling stations sold single-use bottles.
options.B: Students stopped drinking water at school.
options.C: The gym and cafeteria were moved to new buildings.
options.D: Convenient refill access encouraged reusable-bottle use.

questions.explanation: D is correct. More refilling and fewer disposable purchases imply a substitution enabled by access.

questions.stem: A shipping company redesigned a box so that its flaps locked without tape. Packing time decreased, and boxes opened accidentally no more often than before. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: The locking design improved packing efficiency without reducing closure reliability.
options.B: Tape had previously made every box open accidentally.
options.C: The redesigned box required more packing time.
options.D: The company stopped shipping products in boxes.

questions.explanation: A is correct. The two outcomes imply an efficiency gain without a reliability cost.

questions.stem: A theater offered a relaxed performance with softer sound effects and permission for audience members to leave and return. Attendance included more families with sensory-sensitive children than at standard performances. Which statement is most strongly implied by the text?

options.A: Standard performances prohibited all families.
options.B: Modified performance conditions made the theater more accessible to some families.
options.C: The relaxed performance used louder sound effects.
options.D: Audience members were required to remain seated throughout.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The audience difference implies that the accommodations removed barriers for some families.
